los.text: Perform basic life support procedures on an infant and a child in accordance with current guidelines.
los.html:
StepInfant (<1 year)Child (1 year to puberty)
AirwayHead neutral ("sniffing"), chin liftHead tilt, chin lift
5 rescue breaths firstMouth over mouth and noseMouth to mouth (pinch nose)
Check signs of lifeUp to 10 s (brachial pulse for healthcare staff)Up to 10 s (carotid/femoral)
CompressionsTwo thumbs encircling (or two fingers), lower half of sternumOne or two hands, lower half of sternum
DepthAt least one third of chest depth (~4 cm)At least one third (~5 cm)
Ratio15:215:2
Rate100–120/min100–120/min
AloneGive 1 minute of CPR before going for help (paediatric arrests are usually hypoxic), unless a mobile phone is to hand (call on speaker).
GuidelineResuscitation Council UK Paediatric BLS (2021).

los.text: Manage a choking incident in a child using appropriate first aid techniques.
los.html:
1Encourage coughing if the cough is effective; stay with the child.
2. Ineffective cough, conscious
  • Shout for help
  • 5 back blows (infant: face down along your forearm, head low; child: leaning forward) between the shoulder blades.
3Then 5 thrusts: infant: chest thrusts (like compressions, sharper and slower); child: abdominal thrusts (Heimlich).
4Repeat back blows and thrusts, checking for the object after each cycle.
5. UnconsciousOpen the airway, give 5 rescue breaths, start CPR 15:2; look for the object (don't finger sweep blindly).
  • No abdominal thrusts in infants (risk of organ injury).

los.text: Obtain a blood sample from a model while adhering to aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) principles.
los.html:
1Check the request, identify the patient, explain, consent, ask about needle phobia and fainting, allergies (latex, chlorhexidine).
2Hand hygiene, gather equipment on a clean tray (ANTT: protect key parts).
3Apply the tourniquet 7–10 cm above the site (max 1 minute); find a vein (usually median cubital).
4Clean with 2% chlorhexidine/70% alcohol for 30 s, let it dry; don't re-touch (key site).
5Anchor the vein, insert the needle bevel up at 15–30°, attach tubes in the order of draw (blood cultures first, then citrate (blue), serum (red/gold), heparin (green), EDTA (purple), fluoride (grey)).
6Release the tourniquet before removing the needle; apply pressure.
7Dispose of the sharp immediately in a sharps bin; label tubes at the bedside; hand hygiene; document.
  • ANTT: identify key parts (needle, tube connectors) and key sites (skin puncture site) and never touch them.

sessions: Paediatric history taking including developmental history

AgeApproach

PreschoolSimple language, involve with toys; parent gives most history

Adolescent

  • HEADSSS (home, education, activities, drugs, sexuality, suicide/mood, safety) and confidentiality and its limits
